title: How to Use a Dough Scraper for Sourdough Sourdough Rolls
meta_description: Master your sourdough rolls! Learn how to divide sourdough rolls with a dough scraper for perfect portions and a clean workspace. Expert tips inside.
html:
There is nothing quite like the smell of fresh sourdough rolls baking in the oven. But if you've ever tried to portion out a sticky mass of fermented dough with a kitchen knife, you know it can quickly become a messy struggle. The secret to professional, uniform rolls isn't a fancy machine—it's a simple hand tool.

Learning how to divide sourdough rolls dough scraper style is a game-changer for any home baker. A bench scraper allows you to cut through the dough quickly without degassing it too much, ensuring your rolls stay light and airy. If you are just starting out, the 3-in-1 Sourdough Whisk Set (Whisk, Scraper, Lame) is an ideal investment because it gives you the exact tool needed for this stage of the process.

Preparing Your Dough for Dividing

Before you reach for your scraper, make sure your dough has completed its bulk fermentation. Sourdough rolls usually require a slightly tighter crumb than a rustic loaf, so ensure your dough has risen by about 50% to 75% and feels bubbly and alive.

Lightly dust your work surface with rice flour or all-purpose flour. While some bakers prefer a completely naked counter, a light dusting prevents the dough from sticking to the surface, making the dividing process much smoother. Gently tip your dough out of the bowl, using the scraper to help nudge the last few bits of dough onto the bench.

How to Divide Sourdough Rolls with a Dough Scraper

Now comes the part where you divide sourdough rolls dough scraper in hand. Instead of pulling or tearing the dough—which can rip the gluten strands you worked so hard to build—you will use a clean, decisive chopping motion.

Start by shaping your dough into a rough rectangle or log. Use a kitchen scale to weigh the total mass, then divide that number by how many rolls you want. For standard dinner rolls, 60g to 80g per piece is usually perfect. Use the flat edge of the scraper from your 3-in-1 Sourdough Whisk Set to slice the dough into equal strips, then cut those strips into individual portions.

The key is to press straight down. Do not saw back and forth. A single, sharp vertical cut creates a clean edge that is much easier to tension during the shaping phase.

Shaping Your Rolls for Maximum Lift

Once your dough is divided, you need to create surface tension. This is what prevents your rolls from flattening out into pancakes in the oven. Take a piece of divided dough and flip it over so the seam is on the bottom.

Using your palms, gently pull the edges of the dough toward the center, then roll it over itself to create a tight ball. You can use the dough scraper to help you tuck the edges underneath the roll if the dough is particularly sticky. This creates a smooth, rounded top that will expand upward during the oven spring.

Cleaning Your Workspace Efficiently

One of the biggest advantages of using a bench scraper isn't just the cutting—it's the cleanup. Sourdough starter is notorious for sticking to every corner of a countertop. Once your rolls are shaped and tucked into their baking pan, use the scraper to gather all the stray bits of flour and dough.

Instead of scrubbing your counter with a wet sponge (which often just smears the paste around), use the flat blade of the scraper to scrape the surface clean. This pushes all the debris into one pile, which you can then toss in the compost or trash, leaving your kitchen tidy and ready for the next bake.

Essential Tools for the Sourdough Process

While the scraper is the star of the dividing process, sourdough baking is a multi-step journey that requires a few specific tools to get right. If you're building your kit, look for tools that handle the three main phases: mixing, dividing, and scoring.

  • Danish Dough Whisk: Perfect for the initial mix, as it cuts through heavy dough without overworking it.
  • Dough Scraper: Essential for dividing rolls and cleaning your bench.
  • Bread Scoring Lame: Used to create a controlled vent in the dough so it expands evenly.

Getting these tools together in a package, like the 3-in-1 Sourdough Whisk Set, ensures you aren't scrambling for a butter knife or a spatula midway through your bake.

FAQ

Can I use a plastic scraper for dividing sourdough rolls?

Yes, plastic scrapers are great for moving dough and cleaning surfaces, but stainless steel scrapers generally provide a cleaner, sharper cut when dividing portions, which helps preserve the dough's structure.

Why are my sourdough rolls sticking to the scraper?

If the dough is sticking, you can lightly oil the blade of your scraper with a neutral oil or dust it with a bit of flour. This creates a barrier that allows the blade to slide through the dough effortlessly.

Do I need to weigh every single roll?

While not strictly necessary, weighing your rolls ensures they all bake at the same rate. If some are significantly larger than others, the small ones may dry out before the large ones are cooked through.
